descriptionChirho: Kaisar (Caesar), the title and proper name for the Roman emperor, used as a proper noun throughout the NT referring to the reigning Caesar. In the Synoptic 'render unto Caesar' pericope (Matt 22:17,21; Mark 12:14,16-17; Luke 20:22,24-25), it denotes the Roman authority to whom taxes are owed. In Luke 2:1 and 3:1 it refers specifically to Augustus and Tiberius. In John 19:12,15, the Jewish leaders invoke Caesar against Jesus. In Acts 17:7, 25:8-12,21, 26:32, 27:24, 28:19, Paul appeals to Caesar (Nero). Phil 4:22 mentions 'Caesar's household.' Cross-linguistically monolithic: Arabic Qaysar, German Casar/Kaiser, Hebrew Qeisar, Hindi Kaisar, Korean Gaisa, Spanish Kaisar/Cesar, French Cesar. The four auto-clusters merely split case forms (accusative, dative, genitive) and minor English gloss variants ('Caesar' vs 'Kaisar' vs 'of Caesar') -- all inflectional variants of a single proper-noun sense.
